substantive_delta: The proof resolves every ell>=1 and every host size in immutable Problem3.23, strengthening its local assertion to an exact global weighted-host inequality. It also characterizes equality and proves a dimension-free spectral forcing modulus with exponent4ell, shown optimal by the regular three-vertex family. The central square-norm certificate is dimension independent and requires neither entrywise positivity nor a small skew perturbation.
why_nonroutine: The classical block reduction is credited rather than claimed as new. The first-power norm bound cannot be squared to give a lower bound for the square, and T^2 leaves the almost-skew class. The candidate supplies an explicit Rayleigh vector with a nonnegative residual identity, followed by a separate two-dimensional min-max argument for the second eigenvalue. The verified asymmetric transfer lacks its edge-homomorphism hypothesis; the verified coefficient test stops applying at length16. No equivalent full-family implication was identified in the inspected current primary sources, so this is not assessed as an elementary corollary of an identified prior theorem.
significance: An entire infinite family explicitly left unresolved even locally in a recent primary source is settled globally, uniformly over nonregular weighted hosts and all dimensions. The argument replaces cycle-by-cycle coefficient testing with one reusable matrix-square inequality and adds optimal-exponent quantitative forcing. This is substantive mathematical value independent of proof length; it does not by itself establish STOC quality or acceptance.
